title: A Tower That Was Both Lighthouse and Minaret | China Travel Expert
description:
For 1,300 years this Guangzhou tower guided ships home — yet it was never built as a lighthouse.

Huaisheng Mosque was founded in the early Tang dynasty, one of the oldest mosques in China. Its 36m smooth brick “Guang Ta” is a minaret — built to call the faithful to prayer — but sailors on the Maritime Silk Road used it as a navigation beacon: a flag by day, a lamp by night told them they’d reached Guangzhou. Tradition credits an Arab merchant with its founding. It sits on China’s UNESCO tentative list.

🧭 Expert Tip: It’s a working mosque — check prayer times, dress modestly, and be quiet inside the courtyard.

一座塔，白天挂旗、夜里点灯，既是宣礼塔，又是海丝路上的灯塔。
